facts.statement: Lonchodytes likely lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived probably during the Maastrichtian, 70 million years ago (mya)

facts.statement: It is debated whether the fossils found in the Lance Creek Formation are in situ or reworked from younger Danian deposits.
facts.quote: though it seems still somewhat unclear if it did fossilize there or was reworked from later (Danian: Early Paleocene, less than 65 mya) deposits

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggests Lonchodytes is more closely related to Procellariiformes (tubenoses) than to other bird orders.
facts.quote: It was found to be closer to Procellariiformes than to the other orders by a cladistic analysis

facts.statement: Researchers generally believe Lonchodytes is closely related to, or part of a clade with, other higher waterbirds like penguins.
facts.quote: These are today generally believed to be closely related if not actually a clade, perhaps together with other "higher waterbirds" such as penguins

facts.statement: Lonchodytes is classified within the parent group Aequornithes.
Lonchodytes estesi is the type species of the genus Lonchodytes.
The genus Lonchodytes existed from 72.2 to 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
